# Embodied Harnesses

> Systems where an LLM/VLM-driven agent loop orchestrates robot capabilities (skills, VLAs, motion primitives, generated code) and closes the loop on feedback.  
> Layer: L4 · 160 entries · [overview](../README.md#harness) · [survey](../SURVEY.md)

**Legend:** 🟢 open · 🟡 partial · 🔵 api · ⚪ closed. Hover a name for the full paper title. Newest first within each year.

**2026**

- ⚪ [**Skill2Real**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02788 "Skill2Real: Agentic Skill Learning for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Robot Manipulation") · 2026-10 — Frontier-model agents learn executable skills against a shared robot API through a Proposer-Verifier-Governor loop that uses privileged simulation evidence to validate updates; a Cerebellum skill memory and a Brain composition memory transfer to a real robot without fine-tuning.
- ⚪ [**RPG**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02204 "Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents") · 2026-10 — Improves a multimodal-LLM robot execution system without weight updates: it builds simulated practice tasks from an offline dataset, diagnoses failures with execution feedback and privileged state, then creates or refines symbolic skills and revises the system prompt, keeping only changes that pass cross-task checks. [project](https://rpg-robot.github.io/)
- ⚪ [**RoboBridge**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02717 "RoboBridge: A Self-Evolving Embodied Agent Framework for Sim-to-Real Transfer") · 2026-10 — Treats sim-to-real transfer as continued adaptation of executable task skills: a tool-using agent represents tasks as procedures linking intent, observations, tool operations and outcome verification, and revises them from interaction feedback in simulation and reality.
- ⚪ [**Recova**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01178 "Recova: Agent-Guided Failure Recovery for Autonomous Robotic Manipulation") · 2026-10 — Agent-guided framework that develops task and recovery behaviours in a reconstructed digital twin, then monitors deployment, invokes learned or programmatic recoveries, verifies scene restoration and routes real rollouts and human fixes into DAgger training. [project](https://www.liuisabella.com/Recova)

- 🟡 [**MobiAgent**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03476 "MobiAgent: Dual-Loop Recursive Policy Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation") · 2026-10 — Dual-loop agent for long-horizon mobile manipulation: an inner loop uses a VLM for receding-horizon planning and visual reflection over composable atomic skills, run by flow-matching experts on a shared VLM backbone; an outer loop drives lifelong policy self-improvement. _Note: CoRL 2026. Lessons from 123 Rounds of Agentic Skill Discovery") · 2026-09 · National University of Singapore — Report on an agent that watches a robot fail, writes skills or installs models, tests in simulation and repeats for 123 rounds; gains did not compound, with bottlenecks in relational perception, skill chains that stall early, and the harness's evaluator and memory. _Note: Single-author technical report; a negative-results case study._

- 🟢 [**LABOR**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02018 "Large Language Models for Orchestrating Bimanual Robots") · 2024-04 · University of Hamburg — LLM agent that analyzes task configurations and generates coordination control policies for long-horizon bimanual tasks, evaluated in simulation on the NICOL humanoid with a failure-case analysis. [code](https://github.com/Kchu/LABOR-Agent) · [project](https://labor-agent.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**DELTA**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.03275 "DELTA: Decomposed Efficient Long-Term Robot Task Planning using Large Language Models") · 2024-04 · Bosch; University of Stuttgart — Uses LLMs with 3D scene graphs to generate PDDL domain and problem files, prune task-irrelevant graph items, and decompose long-term goals into an autoregressive sequence of sub-goals solved by a classical planner. [code](https://github.com/boschresearch/DELTA) · [project](https://delta-llm.github.io/)
- ⚪ [**COME-robot**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10220 "Closed-Loop Open-Vocabulary Mobile Manipulation with GPT-4V") · 2024-04 · BIGAI — Closed-loop GPT-4V system for open-vocabulary mobile manipulation with multi-level perception for exploration and target identification, plus a feedback-and-restoration loop that checks feasibility, monitors execution and traces failure causes for recovery. [project](https://come-robot.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**LLM^3**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.11552 "LLM3: Large Language Model-based Task and Motion Planning with Motion Failure Reasoning") · 2024-03 · UCLA; BIGAI — LLM-based task-and-motion planning in which the LLM proposes symbolic action sequences and continuous parameters, then iteratively refines them by reasoning over motion-planning failure feedback returned through the prompt. [code](https://github.com/AssassinWS/LLM-TAMP)
- 🟢 [**BTGenBot**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12761 "BTGenBot: Behavior Tree Generation for Robotic Tasks with Lightweight LLMs") · 2024-03 · Politecnico di Milano — Fine-tunes LLMs of at most 7B parameters (Llama-2 chat, CodeLlama) on a GPT-3.5-built dataset to generate robot behavior trees, checked by static analysis, a validator, simulation and a real robot; dataset and LoRA adapters released. [code](https://github.com/AIRLab-POLIMI/BTGenBot)
- 🟢 [**AutoGPT+P**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10778 "AutoGPT+P: Affordance-based Task Planning with Large Language Models") · 2024-02 · KIT (H2T) — Derives the planning domain from an affordance-based scene representation (object detection plus ChatGPT-generated object-affordance mappings) and runs an LLM-driven planning tool with error correction that can also explore, suggest alternatives or return partial plans. [code](https://git.h2t.iar.kit.edu/birr/autogpt-p-standalone)
- ⚪ [**RePLan**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.04157 "RePLan: Robotic Replanning with Perception and Language Models") · 2024-01 · University of Toronto; Vector Institute; Georgia Tech; NVIDIA — Uses a VLM's grounded understanding of world state to detect when an LLM-generated plan (with LLM-generated low-level rewards) fails to reach its goal and to replan online; introduces an eight-task Reasoning and Control (RC) benchmark. [project](https://replan-lm.github.io/replan.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**OK-Robot**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.12202 "OK-Robot: What Really Matters in Integrating Open-Knowledge Models for Robotics") · 2024-01 · NYU; Meta — Training-free open-knowledge system that combines VLM-based object detection and semantic memory with navigation and grasping primitives for open-vocabulary pick-and-drop in homes; 58.5% success across 10 real homes (first-party). _Note: Modular VLM pipeline rather than an LLM agent loop; included as a foundational open-knowledge integration study._ [code](https://github.com/ok-robot/ok-robot) · [project](https://ok-robot.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**MapGPT**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.07314 "MapGPT: Map-Guided Prompting with Adaptive Path Planning for Vision-and-Language Navigation") · 2024-01 · HKU; Sun Yat-sen University; Meituan — Zero-shot VLN agent that feeds GPT-4/GPT-4V an online linguistic map of nodes and topology plus an adaptive multi-step path-planning mechanism, improving zero-shot success on R2R and REVERIE (first-party). [code](https://github.com/chen-judge/MapGPT) · [project](https://chen-judge.github.io/MapGPT/)

**2023**

- 🟢 [**TypeFly**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14950 "TypeFly: Flying Drones with Large Language Model") · 2023-12 · Yale University — LLM drone-control system in which the model writes plans in MiniSpec, a token-efficient language that is interpreted while it streams, over a skill set and a YOLO-based scene description, cutting response time by up to 62% (first-party). [code](https://github.com/typefly/TypeFly) · [project](https://typefly.github.io/)
- ⚪ [**Alter3 (GPT-4)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.06571 "From Text to Motion: Grounding GPT-4 in a Humanoid Robot 'Alter3'") · 2023-12 · University of Tokyo; Alternative Machine — Maps GPT-4's linguistic descriptions of human actions onto the Alter3 android's body through generated program code, producing poses and motion sequences zero-shot and adjusting them from verbal feedback. [project](https://tnoinkwms.github.io/ALTER-LLM/)
- ⚪ [**ViLa**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17842 "Look Before You Leap: Unveiling the Power of GPT-4V in Robotic Vision-Language Planning") · 2023-11 · Tsinghua University — Uses GPT-4V directly as the robot task planner, reasoning over camera images to emit actionable steps, accepting multimodal goal specifications, and incorporating visual feedback to re-plan in real and simulated open-world manipulation. [project](https://robot-vila.github.io/)
- ⚪ [**RoboGPT**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.15649 "RoboGPT: an intelligent agent of making embodied long-term decisions for daily instruction tasks") · 2023-11 · CASIA — Agent pairing a Llama planner fine-tuned on a 67k-task robotic dataset (with a low-cost re-plan module) with RoboSkill navigation and manipulation skills per sub-goal; outperforms prior methods on ALFRED (first-party). _Note: Paper states code and dataset 'will be released soon'; not found as of 2026-09._
- ⚪ [**REAL**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01403 "REAL: Resilience and Adaptation using Large Language Models on Autonomous Aerial Robots") · 2023-11 · MIT — Places an offboard LLM (queried at 0.1-1 Hz) in a multirotor's mission-planning and control loops to supply prior knowledge, interpret logs and diagnostics, and adapt control inputs; real flights show reduced position-tracking error.
- 🟡 [**GPT-4V(ision) for Robotics**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12015 "GPT-4V(ision) for Robotics: Multimodal Task Planning from Human Demonstration") · 2023-11 · Microsoft — GPT-4V describes a human demonstration video, GPT-4 turns it into a symbolic task plan, and vision modules ground grasp/release moments and affordances (grasp types, waypoints) so real robots can execute from one-shot demonstrations. _Note: Repository contains prompts and sample code for the task-recognition stage only._ [code](https://github.com/microsoft/GPT4Vision-Robot-Manipulation-Prompts) · [project](https://microsoft.github.io/GPT4Vision-Robot-Manipulation-Prompts/)
- 🟢 [**DROC**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.10678 "Distilling and Retrieving Generalizable Knowledge for Robot Manipulation via Language Corrections") · 2023-11 · Stanford University — LLM-based system that responds to online language corrections at both plan and skill-parameter level, distills them into a knowledge base, and retrieves relevant past corrections by textual and visual similarity when facing new tasks. [code](https://github.com/Stanford-ILIAD/droc) · [project](https://sites.google.com/stanford.edu/droc)
- 🟢 [**Agent-Driver**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.10813 "A Language Agent for Autonomous Driving") · 2023-11 · USC; Stanford University; NVIDIA — Recasts the driving pipeline as an LLM agent with a function-call tool library, a cognitive memory of common sense and past experience, and a reasoning engine for chain-of-thought, task and motion planning and self-reflection; evaluated on nuScenes. [code](https://github.com/physical-superintelligence-lab/Agent-Driver) · [project](https://psi-lab.ai/Agent-Driver/)
- ⚪ [**Tree-Planner**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08582 "Tree-Planner: Efficient Close-loop Task Planning with Large Language Models") · 2023-10 · HKU; Shanghai AI Laboratory — Splits closed-loop LLM task planning into plan sampling, action-tree construction and grounded top-down decisions with backtracking, cutting token consumption by 92.2% versus the previous best-performing method (first-party).
- ⚪ [**RoboTool**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.13065 "Creative Robot Tool Use with Large Language Models") · 2023-10 · CMU; Google DeepMind — LLM pipeline with Analyzer, Planner, Calculator and Coder modules that turns instructions into executable robot code for tasks with implicit physical constraints that require creative tool use, in simulation and on real robots. [project](https://creative-robotool.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**ITP**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10645 "Interactive Task Planning with Language Models") · 2023-10 · UC Berkeley — Couples LLM high-level planning with low-level skill execution through function calling and grounds the scene in language with pretrained vision models; replans mid-execution when users send new requests, shown on a real milk-tea-making robot. _Note: Published in TMLR (2025)._ [code](https://github.com/Boyiliee/ITP) · [project](https://wuphilipp.github.io/itp_site/)
- 🟢 [**HELPER**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.15127 "Open-Ended Instructable Embodied Agents with Memory-Augmented Large Language Models") · 2023-10 · CMU — Parses free-form human-robot dialogue into action programs via retrieval-augmented prompting over an external memory of language-program pairs that grows during deployment to personalize to users; state of the art on TEACh (first-party). [code](https://github.com/Gabesarch/HELPER) · [project](https://helper-agent-llm.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**CoPAL**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.07263 "CoPAL: Corrective Planning of Robot Actions with Large Language Models") · 2023-10 · Honda Research Institute Europe — Architecture linking reasoning, planning and motion generation with a replanning loop that feeds physically grounded, logical and semantic plan errors back to the LLM; evaluated in simulation and real blocks-world, barman and pizza-preparation scenarios. [code](https://github.com/HRI-EU/Loom) · [project](https://hri-eu.github.io/Loom/)
- ⚪ [**SayNav**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.04077 "SayNav: Grounding Large Language Models for Dynamic Planning to Navigation in New Environments") · 2023-09 · SRI International — Incrementally builds a 3D scene graph of the explored area as LLM context to generate and continually refine step-by-step navigation plans, executed by a pretrained point-goal planner; evaluated on multi-object navigation in ProcTHOR houses. [project](https://www.sri.com/publication/saynav-grounding-large-language-models-for-dynamic-planning-to-navigation-in-new-environments/)
- 🟢 [**DiLu**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16292 "DiLu: A Knowledge-Driven Approach to Autonomous Driving with Large Language Models") · 2023-09 · Shanghai AI Laboratory — Closed-loop LLM driver agent with Reasoning and Reflection modules and a growing memory of past driving experience; makes common-sense decisions in the highway-env simulator and generalizes better than RL baselines (first-party). _Note: Evaluated in highway-env (an abstracted traffic simulator), not on a physical vehicle; ICLR 2024._ [code](https://github.com/PJLab-ADG/DiLu) · [project](https://pjlab-adg.github.io/DiLu/)
- 🟢 [**SayCanPay**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.12682 "SayCanPay: Heuristic Planning with Large Language Models using Learnable Domain Knowledge") · 2023-08 — Combines LLM action generation (Say) with learned estimators of feasibility (Can) and long-term payoff (Pay) inside heuristic search to produce plans that are both grounded and cost-effective. [code](https://github.com/RishiHazra/saycanpay) · [project](https://rishihazra.github.io/SayCanPay/)
- 🟢 [**VoxPoser**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.05973 "VoxPoser: Composable 3D Value Maps for Robotic Manipulation with Language Models") · 2023-07 · Stanford University — An LLM writes code that queries a VLM to compose 3D affordance and constraint value maps in the robot's observation space; a model-based planner uses them to synthesize closed-loop 6-DoF end-effector trajectories zero-shot. _Note: Released code is the RLBench implementation; the real-world perception pipeline is not included._ [code](https://github.com/huangwl18/VoxPoser) · [project](https://voxposer.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**AutoTAMP**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.06531 "AutoTAMP: Autoregressive Task and Motion Planning with LLMs as Translators and Checkers") · 2023-06 · MIT; Harvard University — Few-shot LLM translation of natural-language tasks into an intermediate task representation that a TAMP algorithm solves jointly with motion, with autoregressive re-prompting that detects and corrects syntactic and semantic translation errors. [code](https://github.com/yongchao98/AutoTAMP) · [project](https://yongchao98.github.io/MIT-REALM-AutoTAMP/)
- 🟢 [**TidyBot**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.05658 "TidyBot: Personalized Robot Assistance with Large Language Models") · 2023-05 · Princeton University; Stanford University; Google — Uses LLM few-shot summarization to infer generalizable user preferences for where objects belong from a handful of examples, combined with language-based planning and perception on a real mobile manipulator that tidies rooms. [code](https://github.com/jimmyyhwu/tidybot) · [project](https://tidybot.cs.princeton.edu/)
- 🟢 [**NavGPT**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16986 "NavGPT: Explicit Reasoning in Vision-and-Language Navigation with Large Language Models") · 2023-05 · University of Adelaide — Purely LLM-based VLN agent that, at each step, reasons over textual descriptions of observations, navigation history and explorable directions, showing explicit sub-goal planning and progress tracking; zero-shot R2R results still trail trained models. [code](https://github.com/GengzeZhou/NavGPT)
- 🟢 [**Instruct2Act**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.11176 "Instruct2Act: Mapping Multi-modality Instructions to Robotic Actions with Large Language Model") · 2023-05 · Shanghai AI Laboratory — An LLM writes Python programs that call perception APIs backed by foundation models (SAM to locate objects, CLIP to classify them) and robot action primitives, mapping multimodal instructions to tabletop manipulation zero-shot. [code](https://github.com/OpenGVLab/Instruct2Act)
- 🟢 [**Demo2Code**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16744 "Demo2Code: From Summarizing Demonstrations to Synthesizing Code via Extended Chain-of-Thought") · 2023-05 · Cornell University — Generates robot task code from demonstrations by recursively summarizing them into a concise latent specification and then recursively expanding code functions from it; evaluated on robot task benchmarks including the Robotouille cooking game. [code](https://github.com/portal-cornell/demo2code) · [project](https://portal-cornell.github.io/demo2code/)
- ⚪ [**LLM-Brain**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.09349 "LLM as A Robotic Brain: Unifying Egocentric Memory and Control") · 2023-04 — Uses an LLM as the robot's brain in closed-loop, multi-round natural-language dialogues among multimodal models covering perception, planning, control and egocentric memory; demonstrated on active exploration and embodied question answering. _Note: Later integrated into 'Mindstorms in Natural Language-Based Societies of Mind' (arXiv 2305.17066)._
- 🟢 [**LLM+P**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.11477 "LLM+P: Empowering Large Language Models with Optimal Planning Proficiency") · 2023-04 · UT Austin — The LLM translates a natural-language planning problem into PDDL, a classical planner solves it, and the plan is translated back to language, giving correct or optimal plans on problems where LLMs alone fail to find feasible ones. [code](https://github.com/Cranial-XIX/llm-pddl)
- 🟢 [**ChatGPT Long-Step Robot Control**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03893 "ChatGPT Empowered Long-Step Robot Control in Various Environments: A Case Application") · 2023-04 · Microsoft — Few-shot ChatGPT prompts that turn instructions into sequences of predefined robot actions, represent the environment in a formalized style and infer its updated state; users adjust the output with natural-language feedback before execution. [code](https://github.com/microsoft/ChatGPT-Robot-Manipulation-Prompts)
- ⚪ [**Text2Motion**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12153 "Text2Motion: From Natural Language Instructions to Feasible Plans") · 2023-03 · Stanford University — Guides LLM task planning with feasibility heuristics from the Q-functions of a skill library and runs geometric feasibility planning across whole skill sequences, returning task- and motion-level plans verified to reach inferred symbolic goals. [project](https://sites.google.com/stanford.edu/text2motion)
- 🟢 [**Matcha**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.08268 "Chat with the Environment: Interactive Multimodal Perception Using Large Language Models") · 2023-03 · University of Hamburg — LLM-backboned interactive-perception agent that issues epistemic actions to sample vision, sound, haptic and proprioceptive feedback in a partially observable task, reasons over the returned descriptions, and then plans the task execution. [code](https://github.com/xf-zhao/Matcha) · [project](https://matcha-agent.github.io/)
- ⚪ [**LLM-GROP**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.06247 "Task and Motion Planning with Large Language Models for Object Rearrangement") · 2023-03 · SUNY Binghamton; Meta AI — Prompts an LLM for commonsense, semantically valid object configurations and instantiates them with a task and motion planner that adapts to scene geometry, turning language commands into human-aligned rearrangements on a real mobile manipulator. [project](https://sites.google.com/view/llm-grop)
- ⚪ [**Grounded Decoding**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.00855 "Grounded Decoding: Guiding Text Generation with Grounded Models for Embodied Agents") · 2023-03 · Robotics at Google — Treats LLM planning like probabilistic filtering: decodes action sequences that are likely under the LLM and also under grounded models of the environment (e.g., affordance or safety objectives), solving long-horizon tasks across three simulated and real robot domains. [project](https://grounded-decoding.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**ChatGPT for Robotics (PromptCraft)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.17582 "ChatGPT for Robotics: Design Principles and Model Abilities") · 2023-02 · Microsoft — Study of driving robots with ChatGPT via prompt-engineering principles and a high-level robot function library, using dialogue for closed-loop correction and code synthesis across drones, manipulators and embodied agents; released PromptCraft with a sample simulator integration. _Note: Blog post and arXiv v1 both dated 2023-02-20 (despite the 2306 arXiv identifier)._ [code](https://github.com/microsoft/PromptCraft-Robotics) · [blog](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/articles/chatgpt-for-robotics/)

**2022**

- 🟢 [**LLM-Planner**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04088 "LLM-Planner: Few-Shot Grounded Planning for Embodied Agents with Large Language Models") · 2022-12 · Ohio State University — Uses an LLM as a few-shot high-level planner for embodied instruction following and grounds it by re-planning with objects observed in the environment; competitive on ALFRED with under 0.5% of the paired training data (first-party). [code](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/LLM-Planner) · [project](https://dki-lab.github.io/LLM-Planner/)
- ⚪ [**CAPE**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09935 "CAPE: Corrective Actions from Precondition Errors using Large Language Models") · 2022-11 · Brown University; UT Austin — When an LLM-planned action fails its precondition check, CAPE re-prompts the LLM with the precondition error to propose corrective actions instead of blindly retrying; improves plan correctness over SayCan in VirtualHome and on a Boston Dynamics Spot (first-party). [project](https://shreyas-s-raman.github.io/CAPE/)
- 🟢 [**COWP**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.01287 "Robot Task Planning and Situation Handling in Open Worlds") · 2022-10 · SUNY Binghamton — Open-world task planner that augments a classical planner's action knowledge with task-oriented common sense queried from an LLM when unforeseen execution-time situations break a plan; evaluated on 561 dining-domain situations and on a mobile manipulator. [code](https://github.com/yding25/GPT-Planner) · [project](https://cowplanning.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**ProgPrompt**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.11302 "ProgPrompt: Generating Situated Robot Task Plans using Large Language Models") · 2022-09 · USC; NVIDIA — Prompts LLMs with program-like specifications of the available actions and objects plus example programs, so generated plans are executable in the current environment; state-of-the-art on VirtualHome tasks (first-party) and deployed on a physical tabletop arm. [code](https://github.com/NVlabs/progprompt-vh) · [project](https://progprompt.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**Code as Policies**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.07753 "Code as Policies: Language Model Programs for Embodied Control") · 2022-09 · Robotics at Google — Few-shot prompts code-writing LLMs to generate Python policy code that processes perception outputs and parameterizes control-primitive APIs, with hierarchical generation of undefined functions; demonstrated on multiple real robot platforms. _Note: Released code is a set of Colabs incl. an interactive simulated tabletop domain._ [code](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/code_as_policies) · [project](https://code-as-policies.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**LM-Nav**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.04429 "LM-Nav: Robotic Navigation with Large Pre-Trained Models of Language, Vision, and Action") · 2022-07 · UC Berkeley; Google — Builds a language-guided navigation system entirely from pretrained models without fine-tuning: GPT-3 extracts landmarks from instructions, CLIP grounds them in images, and the ViNG navigation model executes long-horizon outdoor routes on a real robot. [code](https://github.com/blazejosinski/lm_nav) · [project](https://sites.google.com/view/lmnav)
- ⚪ [**Inner Monologue**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.05608 "Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models") · 2022-07 · Robotics at Google — Closes the loop for LLM planners by feeding textual environment feedback (success detection, scene description, human answers) back into the prompt, so the model re-plans; tested on simulated and real tabletop rearrangement and real kitchen mobile manipulation. [project](https://innermonologue.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**Socratic Models**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.00598 "Socratic Models: Composing Zero-Shot Multimodal Reasoning with Language") · 2022-04 · Google — Modular framework that composes pretrained VLMs, LMs and audio models zero-shot by having them exchange information through language prompts; applications include egocentric video QA, assistive dialogue that calls external APIs, and robot perception and planning. [code](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/socraticmodels) · [project](https://socraticmodels.github.io/)
- 🟡 [**SayCan**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.01691 "Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances") · 2022-04 · Robotics at Google; Everyday Robots — An LLM scores candidate natural-language skills for usefulness while pretrained skill value functions score their feasibility in the current state, so the robot executes plans that are both relevant and possible; demonstrated on long-horizon real mobile manipulation. _Note: Released code is a self-contained simulated tabletop implementation; the real-robot skills and value functions are not released._ [code](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/saycan) · [project](https://say-can.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**LM Zero-Shot Planners**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.07207 "Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners: Extracting Actionable Knowledge for Embodied Agents") · 2022-01 · UC Berkeley; CMU; Google — Shows that large LMs prompted with examples can decompose high-level household tasks into mid-level step plans, and adds a procedure that semantically translates each generated step into an admissible environment action; evaluated in VirtualHome. [code](https://github.com/huangwl18/language-planner) · [project](https://wenlonghuang.com/language-planner/)
